mechanism_narrative: A rise in GDP above its 50-day moving average signals increased economic activity, leading to higher demand for goods and services, which in turn drives up S&P 500 prices over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of GDP growth above its 50-day moving average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate below 0.5% signals an accommodative monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing and spending, which drives up S&P 500 prices over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate below 4% signals a tight labor market, leading to increased wage pressure and higher production costs, which drives down S&P 500 prices over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of low unemployment (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts above its 200-day moving average, combined with a rise in consumer spending, signals increased economic activity, leading to higher demand for goods and services, which in turn drives up S&P 500 prices over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of increased housing starts and consumer spending (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production above its 50-day moving average signals increased supply, leading to higher production and lower prices, which drives down S&P 500 prices over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of high industrial production (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the consumer price index above its 200-day moving average, combined with an increase in the federal funds rate, signals higher inflation expectations and tighter monetary policy, leading to lower S&P 500 prices over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment above its 50-day moving average signals a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and higher demand for goods and services, which drives up S&P 500 prices over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of high payroll employment growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate below 1%, combined with an increase in housing starts, signals increased economic activity and higher demand for goods and services, leading to higher S&P 500 prices over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of low interest rates and high housing starts (t-test p > 0.05).
